catalog_entry.label: CBB next permanent head coach (Men's College Basketball Next Coach)
catalog_entry.target: Identity of the next permanent head coach named by a programme (multi-outcome, No-all if none by deadline)
catalog_entry.mechanism: The outcome is an institutional choice: a vacancy opens, an athletic director (with president, board and often a search firm) builds a candidate list from sitting head coaches, assistants and former players, ranks them on track record, ties and fit, and must win a two-sided negotiation constrained by salary, buyouts, roster budget and each candidate's own season calendar. Reports leak along the way. Settlement counts only a permanent (non-interim) hire before the deadline, so unlisted candidates and interim-only outcomes carry probability mass that all listed markets lose. The blueprint season_outcome is kept only because the catalog schema requires an existing blueprint; this archetype takes none of that blueprint's bracket or committee inputs except through the explicitly listed ones (ratings and bracket simulation are used only to score an interim coach's season and a candidate's elimination date).

inputs.why: Search stage and decision-makers bound timing and how open the candidate set still is.
Calibrated insider reports are the main information arriving during a search.
Programme-building record is how committees rank candidates.
Mass on unlisted candidates and on no permanent hire caps listed probabilities.
Alumni, former-staff and AD links are a strong prior on who is chosen.
Salary, buyout capacity and roster budget decide which candidates are reachable.
Candidate's own season or buyout dates can remove him from a fast search.
Show-cause orders and investigations remove otherwise strong candidates.
General coaching news feed captures vacancy openings and announcements with timestamps.
Point-in-time team ratings are the raw basis for a candidate's measured programme improvement.
Defines permanent versus interim, the Sep 1, 2027 cutoff and No-for-all handling.
Interim coach's results versus a fundamentals-only expectation drive the interim-to-permanent route for this vacancy.
Fundamentals-only pregame expected margins and ratings score the interim's season against expectation without any betting line.
Simulated conference finish, NCAA bid and advancement for the interim's team, and elimination dates of candidates' teams.
Preseason expectation baseline for the interim's team, needed to tell over-performance from inherited talent.
Incumbent departure hazard and succession arrangements set the no-vacancy and coach-in-waiting mass for series opened before a vacancy.

interactions.hypothesis: A finalist or offer report late in a search converts to a hire far more often than the same report in the first days after the opening.
Strong-record sitting coaches are reachable only when offer capacity covers salary plus buyout; below that ratio track record stops mattering.
A candidate still coaching in March loses probability as the transfer-portal window approaches if the school's search is already advanced.
A deferred search lets the interim's season results move his hire probability; with an immediate search they do not matter.

contract.settlement_definition: Each market is one candidate for one programme (sample: Oregon men's basketball, candidate Yasir Rosemond). YES if that person is the next permanent (non-interim) head coach of the programme. Interim appointments do not count. If no permanent head coach is selected before Sep 1, 2027, every market in the event resolves No. No game, period, overtime or DNP logic applies. The rules do not name the source of truth (university announcement, board approval or signed contract) nor define the moment of 'selection'.

rules_evidence.quote: This market resolves based on the next permanent (non-interim) head coach of Oregon men's college basketball.
rules_evidence.establishes: Interim or acting appointments are excluded; only the permanent head coach settles a candidate market.

rules_evidence.quote: If no permanent head coach is selected before Sep 1, 2027, all markets resolve to No.
rules_evidence.establishes: A hard cutoff date with a No-for-all outcome, so the no-hire mass is part of the outcome space.

rules_evidence.quote: If the next permanent head coach of Oregon men's college basketball is Yasir Rosemond, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Each market is a single named candidate for a single programme; the series is one multi-outcome event per vacancy.

variants_and_edge_cases: Interim coach later made permanent: the rules settle on the permanent hire, so the interim's own market resolves Yes if the permanent title is conferred before Sep 1, 2027 (the sampled vacancy has an interim coaching 2026-27, so this is the main game-driven route); the transition timing and whether a removed 'interim' tag counts as 'selected' are not specified.
Hire of an unlisted person: rules do not say so explicitly, but each listed market only resolves Yes for its named person, so all listed markets would resolve No.
Agreement reported but not announced, or announced pending board approval before the cutoff and approved after it: 'selected' is undefined in the rules.
Titles such as 'head coach-in-waiting' or co-head coach are not addressed.
Only one series exists (one vacancy sampled); other programmes in the same series would share the template but different cutoff dates may apply.

Series with a sitting coach and no vacancy: the template only fixes Sep 1, 2027 as the cutoff for the Oregon event; if a future market is opened before any vacancy exists, every listed market resolves No unless a vacancy arises and is filled by the cutoff (inference from the No-for-all clause).
Coach-in-waiting or successor named before the vacancy is formal: 'selected' timing is undefined and the named person's market could settle early or on the title conferred.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not stated in the rules; in practice the university's official announcement of the permanent head coach. Kalshi's resolution source for the date of selection is unverified.

mechanism.summary: A next-coach outcome is generated by a hiring process, not by play. A vacancy opens (firing, retirement, departure) and the athletic director, with the president or board and often a search firm, forms a candidate pool: sitting head coaches at lower-resourced or same-tier schools, top assistants and ex-player figures with ties to the programme. Candidates are ranked on programme-building record and fit, filtered by eligibility constraints, and must be reachable: salary plus their current buyout must fit the school's budget, and their own team's postseason or NBA calendar must not collide with the school's need to hire before the transfer portal. The process emits noisy reports with stage-dependent conversion. Settlement is a multi-outcome event over listed names with residual mass on unlisted hires and on no permanent hire before Sep 1, 2027.

stages.name: Vacancy and search set-up
stages.description: The cause of the opening (firing after a poor season, retirement, coach leaving for another job) determines timing, whether a successor was pre-arranged and whether an interim coach is named. The athletic director's tenure, use of a search firm and the governance chain (president, regents) determine speed and how widely the net is cast. The stage of the search at the pricing time decides how much of the outcome remains open. Public reports of 2026-10-07 (KPTV, KATU, AP via OPB) describe the sampled Oregon vacancy: Dana Altman retired effective immediately, assistant Tony Stubblefield is interim for 2026-27 and a national search is planned after the season, so the search start lags the vacancy by about five months; these facts come from news, not from the sampled rules text.
stages.distribution: Time-to-hire counted from the search start is right-skewed: in-season firings of power-conference coaches typically conclude within weeks, while a vacancy with an announced deferred search has a window of months in which no hire is expected; the pre-search window is a separate regime, not the tail of the same distribution.

stages.name: Interim season audition (deferred-search vacancies)
stages.description: When the vacancy is filled by an interim who coaches the whole season and the school defers the search, the team's results between the vacancy and the search start decide whether the interim becomes a front-runner, whether the school cancels the search, and how early or late outside candidates are contacted. The signal is performance against a fundamentals-only expectation, conference finish and NCAA advancement, not raw wins, because the roster was built by the predecessor.
stages.distribution: Mixture: a small point mass on interim-made-permanent when results beat expectation, otherwise a hard reset to a normal search after the season; the interim's probability moves in jumps with the bracket outcome.

stages.name: Candidate pool and ranking
stages.description: The plausible pool is drawn from sitting head coaches whose teams outperformed their resources, top assistants on strong staffs, and people tied to the programme or the athletic director. Ranking weighs measured improvement in adjusted efficiency, NCAA tournament success, recruiting and transfer-portal results, and ties; show-cause orders or open investigations remove names. Unlisted candidates remain possible.
stages.distribution: Probability over identities is concentrated on a few names (top two often hold most mass) with a long tail of plausible others and a non-trivial unlisted residual early in the search.

stages.name: Reachability and negotiation
stages.description: A top-ranked candidate must accept: the offer must exceed salary plus buyout at the current school, roster budget (revenue sharing and NIL) must be competitive, and the current school may counter with an extension. Candidates whose teams are still in the NCAA tournament or whose buyout drops at a later date may be unavailable when the school wants to hire. Competing vacancies at other schools bid for the same people.
stages.distribution: Acceptance is close to binary per candidate given an offer; a declined first choice shifts mass to the next names in a cascade, giving a mixture over orderings.

stages.name: Information release and settlement
stages.description: Insiders report contacts, interviews, finalists, offers and agreements; each stage has a different historical conversion to a hire, and denials carry their own signal. The university announces the hire, sometimes pending board approval. Settlement counts only a permanent coach selected before Sep 1, 2027; interim-only or unlisted outcomes settle every listed market No.
stages.distribution: Information arrives in jumps: one credible agreement report moves a candidate from tens of percent to near certainty; between reports probabilities drift slowly.

talent_strength.note: Candidate quality is the programme-building record, measured from point-in-time ratings.

opponent_matchup.note: Competing vacancies at other schools bid for the same candidates in the same window; no input tracks the simultaneous carousel and the relative attractiveness of rival openings. Stage s3 no longer claims this category; competing vacancies stay a declared gap (coach_u2).

role_personnel.note: Personnel here are the candidates and their ties to the school and the AD.

availability_news.note: Report ledger with conversion rates plus general news feed.

coaching_scheme.note: Analogue only: the athletic director's process (tenure, search firm, governance chain) plays the role of scheme; it describes how the decision is made, not any on-court scheme.

environment.note: Programme resources (salary, buyout capacity, roster budget) are the environment of the hire.

game_context_script.note: No game settles the contract, but the interim's in-season results and NCAA advancement are a path to the permanent job when an interim coaches the season before the search; irrelevant when no interim exists.

pace_volume.note: There is no count of opportunities: the event is a single hiring decision per vacancy, not an accumulation of possessions or attempts.

efficiency_conversion.note: Conversion of report stages (interview, finalist, offer) into hires is the relevant rate.

distribution_variance.note: Multi-outcome identity distribution with unlisted and no-hire residual mass.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Candidate's postseason, NBA and buyout-date timing versus the portal deadline.

officiating_rules.note: Analogue only: NCAA enforcement (show-cause orders, pending infractions) is the governing-rule filter on who can be hired; no officiating or game rule applies to a hiring contract, so this coverage is thin.

settlement_contract.note: Permanent versus interim, cutoff date and No-for-all; selection moment undefined (see unresolved).

cbb.coach_vacancy_search_state.label: Coaching vacancy search state: opening date, decision-makers, search firm and interim arrangement
cbb.coach_vacancy_search_state.mechanism: A hire is the end of a search process run by an athletic director, sometimes a president or board and often a search firm; how far the search has progressed bounds both timing and candidate set.
cbb.coach_vacancy_search_state.rationale: Searches opened by a firing late in a season move fast and usually finish within weeks, but a retirement announced just before a season can be followed by a deliberately deferred search while an interim coaches the whole season; in that regime days since the vacancy carry almost no information and the interim's season does. Subtle: a school can announce the search start in the opening press release, and that single field decides which timing regime applies; the stage of the search (interviews reported, finalist count) then shifts probability between named and unnamed candidates.
cbb.coach_vacancy_search_state.measurement: Per vacancy, as-of timestamp t: opening date and cause (fired, resigned, retired, left for another job), announced search start date or rule ('begins after the season', 'immediately', none stated), search_start_lag = announced search start minus opening date in days, days since the SEARCH opened (floored at 0 while the school says the search has not begun; this, not days since the vacancy, indexes every conversion and residual curve), whether an interim is named, who, and for what span (rest of season or until a hire), AD tenure in years, search firm named (yes/no, which firm), count of publicly reported interviewed candidates and finalists at t, whether a board/regent approval meeting is scheduled; each field carries the first public report timestamp, never backfilled.
raw_data: vacancy table: school, opening_date, cause, interim_coach, interim_span, announced_search_start, AD_name, AD_start_date, search_firm, board_meeting_dates
report log: timestamp, outlet, candidate, stage (contacted/interviewed/finalist/offer)
cbb.coach_vacancy_search_state.why: Defines whether a permanent coach can be named before the Sep 1, 2027 cutoff and how open the candidate set still is.

cbb.coach_candidate_track_record.label: Head-coach candidate track record, opponent-adjusted and resource-adjusted
cbb.coach_candidate_track_record.mechanism: Hiring committees choose among candidates largely on demonstrated programme-building: rating improvement over predecessor, tournament results, recruiting/portal success and conduct record.
cbb.coach_candidate_track_record.rationale: A candidate's raw win-loss record mixes coaching value with programme resources; schools ranking candidates (and reporters naming them) favour coaches whose teams outperform their budget and conference. Subtle: one deep NCAA run inflates perceived value far more than multi-year efficiency gains, so both should be measured.
cbb.coach_candidate_track_record.measurement: For each candidate: seasons as head coach; mean change in adjusted efficiency margin (point-in-time end-of-season Torvik/KenPom) versus the three seasons before arrival; NCAA bids, tournament wins and Sweet 16s in last 5 seasons; resource-adjusted margin = residual of adjusted margin on conference and athletic budget; for assistants: years as top assistant and head-coach tree; shrink single-season effects with weight n/(n+3) seasons.
free_sources: Knight Commission / USA Today athletic finance database
raw_data: coach career table: coach, school, season, role, W-L, tournament result
end-of-season adjusted efficiency margin by team-season
athletic department expenses by school-year
cbb.coach_candidate_track_record.why: Separates candidates a Power-conference school would credibly hire from names floated without a basis.

cbb.candidate_program_ties.label: Candidate ties to the programme, athletic director and conference region
cbb.candidate_program_ties.mechanism: Hires disproportionately go to coaches with prior links: alumni, former assistants of the programme, previous hires of the same AD, coaches already in the region or recruiting footprint.
cbb.candidate_program_ties.rationale: Ties lower information and negotiation costs and are a strong prior over candidate identity; they also explain why a less-accomplished candidate may beat a better record. Subtle: the AD's own career history (schools worked at, previous coaching hires) is often more predictive than the candidate's ties to the school itself.
cbb.candidate_program_ties.measurement: Binary and count features per candidate-school pair: alumnus (played/graduated), former staff member (years, role), previous hire or colleague of the current AD (matched through AD career history), same agent as other staff, head-coaching job within 500 miles or in the same conference footprint; computed from public biographies as of t.
free_sources: Wikipedia coach and AD career pages
raw_data: coach biography: schools, roles, years
AD career history and list of prior coaching hires
agent representation where reported
cbb.candidate_program_ties.why: Prior over which named candidate is chosen; ties often decide among comparable records.

cbb.program_hiring_resources.label: Programme hiring resources: salary pool, buyout capacity, revenue-sharing and NIL budget
cbb.program_hiring_resources.mechanism: Whether a school can land a sitting head coach depends on salary it can offer, its ability to pay that coach's buyout, and the roster budget (revenue sharing and NIL collective) it can promise.
cbb.program_hiring_resources.rationale: Since the 2025 House settlement, roster budget is a central selling point; a sitting coach with a large buyout is only reachable by schools willing to pay it. Subtle: the outgoing coach's own buyout or retirement terms consume the same budget and can push a school toward cheaper assistants.
cbb.program_hiring_resources.measurement: As of t: predecessor's salary and buyout owed (from public contract/FOIA records), reported maximum offer, each candidate's current salary and buyout amount with step-down dates, school athletic revenue (latest fiscal year), basketball share of revenue-sharing allocation where disclosed; express candidate reachability as offer_capacity / (candidate_salary + candidate_buyout).
free_sources: USA Today college basketball coach salary database
raw_data: coach contract table: coach, salary, term, buyout schedule by date
school athletic revenue/expense by fiscal year
reported revenue-sharing and NIL budgets
cbb.program_hiring_resources.why: Rules out candidates the school cannot afford and raises those whose buyout is low or expiring.

cbb.candidate_availability_calendar.label: Candidate availability calendar: current-team season status, buyout step-downs and pro-league timing
cbb.candidate_availability_calendar.mechanism: A candidate coaching a team still alive in the NCAA tournament, an NBA assistant in the playoffs, or one whose buyout drops on a set date is effectively unavailable until that event passes.
cbb.candidate_availability_calendar.rationale: Searches either wait for a preferred candidate or move on; this changes both who is hired and when. Subtle: transfer-portal windows push schools to hire before the portal opens, which penalises candidates whose teams advance deep in March.
cbb.candidate_availability_calendar.measurement: Per candidate as of t: current team's elimination status and earliest elimination date (from bracket simulation), buyout step-down dates and amounts, NBA team playoff status for NBA assistants; per school: transfer-portal opening date and days remaining; feature = expected days until candidate is free versus expected days until school wants a hire.
raw_data: team elimination dates
buyout schedules with dates
transfer-portal calendar
cbb.candidate_availability_calendar.why: Timing constraint that can remove an otherwise preferred candidate from the realistic set.

cbb.coaching_search_report_ledger.label: Timestamped coaching-search report ledger with source reliability and report-to-hire conversion
cbb.coaching_search_report_ledger.mechanism: Insider reports (interviewed, finalist, offer, agreement in principle) are noisy but increasingly informative signals; their historical conversion to actual hires depends on outlet, report stage and lead time.
cbb.coaching_search_report_ledger.rationale: Most of the information about a search arrives as reports, and a single credible agreement report moves the outcome near certainty; but early lists of names include many that never had serious contact. Subtle: candidates and agents leak interest to gain leverage at their current school, so 'interest' reports convert far less than 'finalist' or 'offer' reports.
cbb.coaching_search_report_ledger.measurement: Log every public report with timestamp (UTC), outlet and reporter, candidate, stage in {linked, contacted, interviewed, finalist, offer, agreement, denial}; estimate historical conversion P(hired | stage, outlet tier) from past D1 power-conference searches (at least 5 cycles), shrunk toward stage mean with weight n/(n+10); denial reports from the candidate tracked separately with their own conversion rate.
free_sources: ESPN, CBS Sports and The Athletic reporting
X/Twitter posts of national insiders (capture timestamps)
raw_data: report log: ts, outlet, reporter, candidate, stage, link
hire outcomes per past search
cbb.coaching_search_report_ledger.why: Converts the dominant information stream of a search into calibrated candidate probabilities.

cbb.coach_hire_field_residual.label: Residual probability mass for unlisted candidates and for no permanent hire by the cutoff
cbb.coach_hire_field_residual.mechanism: The multi-outcome contract lists named candidates only; the true distribution includes an 'other' mass (a candidate not listed) and a 'no permanent hire before deadline' mass.
cbb.coach_hire_field_residual.rationale: Listed-candidate probabilities must sum to at most 1 minus these masses; historically many hires are names that were not among the earliest-reported candidates. Subtle: the 'other' mass shrinks quickly as the search progresses and reports concentrate, so it is time-varying.
cbb.coach_hire_field_residual.measurement: From past searches: fraction of hires that were not among the first N publicly linked names at days d since the SEARCH opened (d = 0, 7, 14, 30; the clock is held at 0 until the announced search start, using search_start_lag from the vacancy-state input), estimated as a curve with binomial confidence bands; no-hire mass = P(no vacancy exists by the cutoff, from the incumbent hazard input) + P(search not concluding by Sep 1, 2027 given its start date) + probability that the interim is made permanent (counted for the interim's own market, not for the residual) or that only an interim or coach-in-waiting is named; as-of t.
free_sources: Historical search coverage (ESPN, CBS) reconstructed by date
raw_data: per past search: opening date, candidate link dates, hire identity and date
cbb.coach_hire_field_residual.why: Prevents over-allocating probability to the listed names, which all settle No if someone else is hired.

cbb.candidate_eligibility_constraints.label: Candidate eligibility constraints: NCAA show-cause orders, pending infractions and legal or conduct issues
cbb.candidate_eligibility_constraints.mechanism: A show-cause penalty, pending infractions case or conduct investigation makes most schools unwilling or unable to hire a candidate during its term.
cbb.candidate_eligibility_constraints.rationale: This removes names that a pure track-record ranking would rate highly. Subtle: show-cause orders allow hiring with restrictions, and some schools accept the restrictions; the term end date matters relative to the cutoff.
cbb.candidate_eligibility_constraints.measurement: Per candidate: active NCAA show-cause (start, end, restrictions) from NCAA infractions decisions database; open infractions case flag; public conduct investigations; binary 'constrained at t' and days until constraint lapses.
free_sources: NCAA Legislative Services infractions decisions database
raw_data: infractions decisions: person, penalty, start/end dates
investigation news log
cbb.candidate_eligibility_constraints.why: Filters the candidate set; a constrained candidate is very unlikely to be named permanent coach.

cbb.interim_coach_season_audition.label: Interim coach's in-season audition: results versus preseason expectation and interim-to-permanent base rate
cbb.interim_coach_season_audition.mechanism: When an interim coaches the whole season before the search opens, the team's results under him are the main game-driven route to the permanent job: a clear beat of expectation, a conference finish above projection or an NCAA run turns the interim into a leading candidate or lets the school skip a search.
cbb.interim_coach_season_audition.rationale: Search timing and candidate ranking are set partly by what happens on the court during the deferred-search window. A promoted assistant inherits a roster chosen by the departed coach, so the fair comparison is results against a fundamentals-only expectation, not raw wins; a late-season run also raises the interim's profile with the AD and fan base. Subtle: interim promotions are rare enough that the base rate is tiny-sample, and a poor season can end the interim's case quickly.
cbb.interim_coach_season_audition.measurement: For the interim coach at as-of t: games coached, AdjEM_fund results-versus-expectation = mean over games of (actual margin - cbb.ratings_fundamentals pregame expected margin), shrunk with weight n/(n+12) games toward 0; end-of-season gap between final fundamentals rating and the preseason prior from cbb.preseason_prior; projected conference finish and NCAA bid, seed and round-reached probabilities from cbb.bracket_sim; promotion base rate = share of past D1 interim or acting coaches who coached a full or most of a season (at least 15 games) and were then named permanent, split by whether the team met its preseason expectation (pooled over every available season, shrunk to the pooled mean with weight n/(n+8)); no betting line or price enters any term.
free_sources: Barttorvik T-Rank game results and ratings
Wikipedia and university press releases for historical interim coaches
raw_data: interim coach table: school, season, coach, games_coached, named_permanent flag
game results with pregame fundamentals expected margin
preseason prior rating and final rating by team-season
cbb.interim_coach_season_audition.why: Tells whether the interim's own market (and, by subtraction, every outside candidate's) is driven by the season or by a fresh search; zero relevance only when no interim coaches a meaningful stretch.

cbb.incumbent_coach_departure_hazard.label: Incumbent head-coach departure hazard and succession arrangements
cbb.incumbent_coach_departure_hazard.mechanism: A next-coach market can only pay out after a vacancy exists; before one does, the probability of any listed name is the probability of a vacancy before the cutoff times the conditional hire probability, and a pre-arranged coach-in-waiting changes the conditional distribution.
cbb.incumbent_coach_departure_hazard.rationale: For a template opened on a programme with a sitting coach, the dominant term is the chance the incumbent leaves (retirement, firing, a better job, health), driven by age, contract length, tenure, results against expectation and public succession statements. Subtle: retirements are lumpy around season ends and are often announced with a named successor, which concentrates mass on one name and removes the search entirely.
cbb.incumbent_coach_departure_hazard.measurement: For each sitting head coach at t: age, years remaining on contract, tenure, last three seasons' fundamentals-rating results versus preseason prior, conference and tournament results, reported health or retirement statements, announced coach-in-waiting or succession plan (flag with first report timestamp); hazard h(coach) = logistic fit of departure within 12 months on those covariates over at least 15 past seasons of all D1 head coaches, shrunk toward the age-band base rate with weight n/(n+25) coach-seasons; output P(vacancy opens before the cutoff date) and P(named successor already exists | vacancy).
raw_data: coach-season table: school, coach, age, contract_end, tenure, departure flag and cause
succession announcements with timestamps
cbb.incumbent_coach_departure_hazard.why: Supplies the no-vacancy mass and the coach-in-waiting case that the field-residual input does not cover, needed for any series opened before a vacancy.

cbb.news.reason: The generic coaching/poll/award feed timestamps vacancy openings and official announcements, but it lacks report stage and outlet reliability, which the new report ledger adds.

cbb.point_in_time_rating_snapshot.reason: Needed only as the raw, non-revised rating history used to compute a candidate's improvement over his predecessor; it does not predict the hire by itself.

m.rules_text.reason: The permanent/interim distinction and the Sep 1, 2027 No-for-all cutoff change which outcomes count, so the text must be versioned per market.

cbb.ratings_fundamentals.reason: Supplies the market-free pregame expected margin against which the interim's results are scored; not itself a predictor of the hire.

cbb.bracket_sim.reason: Gives the interim team's projected NCAA bid and advancement, and the earliest elimination date of each candidate's team for the availability calendar.

cbb.preseason_prior.reason: Only the baseline expectation for the interim's team; the audition signal is the gap between results and this prior.

interactions.mechanism: The same report stage converts at different rates depending on search progress: a 'finalist' report two days after a firing is often agent leverage, while one after interviews have closed with a board meeting scheduled is close to decisive.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate hire conversion by report stage split by days-since-opening and by whether a board meeting was scheduled; compare with pooled conversion. Index days by the search start, not the vacancy date, and flag vacancies with an announced deferred start.

interactions.mechanism: Track record raises hire probability only once the school's offer capacity exceeds the candidate's salary plus buyout; below that ratio the strongest records are effectively unattainable and mass moves to assistants.
interactions.how_to_test: Logit of hire on track record interacted with an indicator offer_capacity/(salary+buyout) > 1 across past searches.

interactions.mechanism: Searches either wait for a preferred candidate still coaching in March or close before the transfer portal opens; which regime applies depends on search age and the school's urgency, flipping the candidate's probability.
interactions.how_to_test: Among past searches with a linked candidate still alive in the NCAA tournament, compare hire rates by whether the school had announced an interim and by days to portal opening.

interactions.mechanism: Ties scale the odds of a hire roughly proportionally at any track-record level; an alumnus with a modest record can outrank a stranger with a better one, and an AD's prior hire carries the largest multiplier.
interactions.how_to_test: Conditional logit over candidate sets with track record and tie indicators; test whether tie effects are constant on the odds scale across record quintiles.

interactions.mechanism: Each additional credible report about listed names shrinks the unlisted mass, but the reduction slows as only late surprise hires remain; early surprises are common, late ones rare.
interactions.how_to_test: Plot fraction of hires outside the reported set against cumulative report count and days since opening across past searches.

interactions.mechanism: With a deferred search the interim's results matter only while the search is not yet open: a strong season can cancel or shorten the search (regime A), a weak one hands the decision to a conventional search after the season (regime B), so the interim's hire probability switches level at the search start rather than varying smoothly.
interactions.how_to_test: Among past interim-led seasons, compare promotion rates for teams above and below fundamentals expectation, split by whether the school announced a search for after the season.

interactions.mechanism: The no-hire mass and the unlisted mass are not separable: a retirement with a pre-arranged successor removes both, while a firing opens a conventional search with a large unlisted mass, so the residual masses must be mixed over departure types rather than estimated from all vacancies pooled.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate the unlisted-hire share separately for retirements with named successors, retirements without, and firings, and compare with the pooled figure.

nonlinearities.shape: convex decay in days since the search opened (flat while a deferred search has not started)
nonlinearities.why: Unlisted-candidate mass is roughly constant while the school says the search has not begun, then falls fast in the first week of the real search as names surface and flattens afterwards; a linear decay in days since the vacancy understates the unlisted mass for months in a deferred-search vacancy.
Conversion jumps discretely from 'linked' to 'interviewed' to 'offer' to 'agreement'; agreement reports convert near one, so the response is a staircase, not a smooth curve.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold at offer capacity equal to salary plus buyout
nonlinearities.why: Below the threshold a sitting coach is nearly unreachable; above it extra money adds little because ties and fit dominate.

nonlinearities.shape: step in promotion probability at beating expectation and NCAA bid
nonlinearities.why: Interims who finish near expectation are rarely promoted, while a clear beat plus an NCAA bid makes promotion common; the response is a rise concentrated above a performance threshold rather than proportional to wins.

required_data.grain: one row per public report per candidate per search

catalog_entry.label: CBB overtime periods played
catalog_entry.target: Number of overtime periods played in a game (at least N OT periods)
catalog_entry.mechanism: Reaching N overtime periods requires a tied score at the end of regulation and then N-1 further ties after each five-minute period. The first tie depends on the integer pmf of the regulation margin at zero, set by the strength gap, possessions, three-point lumpiness and end-game decisions; each repeat tie depends on the short-period scoring distribution, which bonus free throws and fouled-out players from foul carryover reshape. Rungs are nested and fall geometrically.

mechanism.summary: The outcome is a count of consecutive ties. Regulation ends tied with a probability equal to the integer pmf of the final margin at zero: it peaks when the expected margin is near zero, decays roughly like a Gaussian in the expected margin over its sd, and the sd scales with the square root of possessions and with three-point lumpiness. Close finishes are strategic: trailing teams choose to play for the tie or the win, leaders up three foul or defend, and holding for the last shot when level converts ties into overtime or wins. Each five-minute overtime has about one-eighth of regulation possessions (5 of 40 minutes), so its own tie probability is materially higher than regulation's, and player fouls and team-foul bonus carry over and make later periods more free-throw driven. Rung N is P(reg tie) times the product of N-1 repeat-tie probabilities, so higher rungs are tiny and very sensitive to the repeat rate.

stages.name: Expected regulation margin
stages.description: The centre of the regulation margin distribution comes from the fundamentals-only strength gap adjusted for home court, neutral site and confirmed absences. Early in the season (such as November buy games between a mid-major and a Big Ten team) the gap is large on average but uncertain, and that uncertainty must be integrated rather than plugged in, because tie probability is a sharply peaked function of the expected margin.
stages.distribution: Expected margin is approximately normal with a standard error that is largest in November and shrinks with games played and schedule connectivity.

stages.name: Width and lumpiness of the regulation margin
stages.description: Around that centre, the spread of possible final margins scales with expected possessions and with the share of scoring that comes in three-point jumps; slow, interior-oriented matchups produce narrow margin distributions and more ties. Because scores are integers built from 1-, 2- and 3-point events, the probability at exactly zero must come from an integer pmf calibrated on observed overtime frequency, not from a continuous density. The first-rung probability is the P_tie_reg term of the existing overtime-chain input, extended as described in its audit entry.
stages.distribution: Discrete margin pmf with sd roughly 10 to 12 points for a 68-possession game; roughly 6 percent of D1 games reach overtime, so P(margin=0) is above that average for evenly matched teams and falls toward 1 percent or less for 15+ point favourites.

stages.name: Strategic final possessions
stages.description: Games within one or two possessions in the final minute are resolved by choices: trailing by two, go for the tie or the win; trailing by three, take a contested three or a quick two and foul; leading by three, foul to prevent a tying three or defend. Intentional fouling and free-throw shooting move the margin in one- and two-point steps. These choices add or remove mass exactly at zero relative to the smooth model.
stages.distribution: Mixture: most games exit this regime before the final minute; within close finishes, the zero point carries an excess or deficit of order tens of percent relative to smoothed neighbours.

stages.name: Repeat ties in five-minute overtime periods
stages.description: Each overtime has about eight to nine possessions per team (one-eighth of a 68-possession game), so the period margin distribution is narrow and a repeat tie is far more likely than a regulation tie. Player fouls and the second-half team-foul count carry into overtime, so bonus free throws are frequent and starters may foul out; fatigue and depleted rotations make later periods differ from the first. Rung N multiplies the regulation tie by N-1 repeat-tie probabilities.
stages.distribution: Geometric-like chain with period-dependent repeat probability (order 10 to 20 percent per period, to be calibrated), so, with a regulation tie near 6 percent, the unconditional 2+ rung is of order 0.6 to 1.2 percent and 3+ of order 0.06 to 0.25 percent, far higher for tied-late even matchups.

stages.name: Settlement on periods played
stages.description: The ladder counts overtime periods played in the official final result. A short postponement keeps the market alive; cancellation or no start within 48 hours settles at a fair price rather than No, removing void risk from the outcome distribution. How a game halted mid-overtime would count is not stated, and the source of the official result is not named.
stages.distribution: Deterministic mapping from the realised count to nested rungs; void mass sits outside the outcome distribution at an undefined fair price.

cbb.endgame_tie_decision_policy.label: Coach end-game decision policy when trailing by 2 or 3 or leading by 3 in the final possessions
cbb.endgame_tie_decision_policy.mechanism: Whether a trailing team goes for the tying two or the winning three, and whether a leader up 3 fouls or defends, decides how much probability lands exactly on a tie at the buzzer.
cbb.endgame_tie_decision_policy.rationale: The tie probability at the end of regulation is not just the density of a smooth margin at zero: in close games the final possessions are strategic, and a coach who reliably plays for overtime raises the tie mass while one who plays for the win shifts it to plus or minus one. Subtle: holding for the last shot when tied converts a tied game into either a win or overtime, so possession at the tie matters.
cbb.endgame_tie_decision_policy.measurement: From play-by-play, for each coach (and pooled by tier): in possessions starting with under 35 seconds left and team trailing by 2, share of final shot attempts that are twos; when trailing by 3, share of threes versus quick twos; when leading by 3 with under 10 seconds, foul rate; shrink coach rates to the pooled rate with weight n/(n+15) situations over the last 5 seasons; convert to a tie-mass multiplier on P(margin=0 at 0:00). Because qualifying situations are only a handful per coach-season, use the tier-level pooled rate by default and let a coach deviate only when his shrunk rate differs from the pooled rate by more than two standard errors.

cbb.ot_foul_carryover_depletion.label: Player-foul and team-foul carryover into overtime and resulting lineup depletion
cbb.ot_foul_carryover_depletion.mechanism: Player fouls and second-half team fouls carry into overtime, so teams entering OT have players near or at the five-foul limit and are already in the bonus, changing scoring variance in each five-minute period.
cbb.ot_foul_carryover_depletion.rationale: Repeat ties depend on how many points are scored per OT period and how lumpy they are: bonus free throws add frequent one- and two-point scores, and fouled-out starters lower efficiency unevenly. Subtle: the carryover makes later OT periods progressively more foul-driven, so per-period tie probability is not constant across periods.
cbb.ot_foul_carryover_depletion.measurement: Rule version assumed (unverified for 2026-27, see ot_u3): men's two 20-minute halves, five personal fouls to disqualify, team-foul bonus carrying from the second half into overtime periods, five-minute overtimes; store a rule_version flag per game and fit only on seasons with the same structure. From play-by-play for all OT games: at the start of each OT period, count players with 4 and 5 fouls per team (weighted by their minutes share), team-foul count and bonus status; points per team per OT period and distribution of scoring events by value; estimate P(tie after OT k | depletion state) by logistic fit pooled over 10 seasons; pregame proxy = team foul rate and bench depth.

cbb.ot_foul_carryover_depletion.why: Explains why the probability of a second or third tie differs from the first and from a constant repeat rate.

cbb.live_game_state_tie_path.label: Live score, clock, period, possession and foul state for in-play overtime pricing
cbb.live_game_state_tie_path.mechanism: Once a game is close late or in overtime, the rung probability is set by the current score difference, time left, possession, team-foul bonus status and players near five fouls, and the pregame margin model becomes nearly irrelevant.
cbb.live_game_state_tie_path.rationale: The 2+ and 3+ rungs sit near zero until regulation is tied or in extra time; if the market trades during the game, almost all price movement comes from the live state. Subtle: a tie at the final buzzer needs both possession and timing, and an overtime already in progress changes the remaining number of required ties by one for each rung; free live feeds can lag, so the data latency itself is a modelling input.
cbb.live_game_state_tie_path.measurement: At as-of t during the game: period, seconds remaining, score margin, possession, team fouls and bonus status for both teams, count of players with 4 fouls and fouled-out players, OT index k already played; P(rung N | state) = P(tie at end of current period | state) x P_tie_OT^(N-k-1) using a state-based first-passage model on the margin (fit on play-by-play with state buckets: margin -6..+6, clock 60 s bins in the last 5 minutes); record feed latency (seconds from event to capture) and discard states older than the latency budget.

cbb.tempo.reason: Margin sd scales with the square root of possessions, so tempo changes tie probability moderately, not as strongly as the strength gap.

cbb.three_pt_dist.reason: Three-point reliance widens and lumps the margin distribution; effect on tie mass is second order relative to expected margin.

interactions.mechanism: Tie probability is a peaked function of the expected margin; averaging it over an uncertain margin raises it for large expected margins (Jensen on the convex tail) and slightly lowers it near zero, so November mismatches carry more OT risk than plug-in estimates suggest.

interactions.mechanism: Margin sd grows with both possessions and three-point share; tie probability scales roughly with the inverse of sd near even games, so slow, low-three matchups compound into the highest regulation tie rates.

interactions.mechanism: End-game policy only matters in games within one or two possessions in the last minute; a play-for-tie coach increases tie mass only in that regime, so its effect scales with the close-game probability.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress OT occurrence on coach policy index interacted with the pregame probability of a within-3 score at the one-minute mark.

interactions.mechanism: Once both teams are in the double bonus with starters fouled out, overtime scoring shifts to free throws and the repeat-tie rate changes; the 3+ rung lives almost entirely in this regime.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate tie-after-OT rate for first versus second and later OT periods and by count of fouled-out starters at period start.

interactions.mechanism: If the leading team's best free-throw shooters are absent, the fouling strategy of the trailing team becomes more effective, increasing comebacks to a tie in the final minute.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare late-game tie conversions when the leader's top ball handlers' FT% is low versus high, conditioning on margin with 60 seconds left.

interactions.mechanism: Intentional fouling by the trailing team pays off in proportion to how often it forces free throws times how poorly the leader's shooters convert; a low-FT% closing lineup facing a foul-heavy trailing coach raises both comeback ties and repeat ties in bonus-heavy OTs.

nonlinearities.shape: Gaussian-shaped decay of tie probability in |expected margin|
nonlinearities.why: Tie probability is flat near zero expected margin and falls off rapidly beyond about one margin sd; a linear OT model on spread overstates OT in mismatches and understates it in pick'em games.
Rung N is proportional to the repeat rate raised to N-1, so a relative error of 20 percent in the repeat rate becomes about 44 percent at 3+ and is the main source of rung mispricing.

nonlinearities.shape: inverse square-root scaling of tie mass in possessions
nonlinearities.why: Margin sd grows like the square root of possessions, so tie probability declines concavely as tempo rises; a 10 percent slower game raises tie mass about 5 percent.

catalog_entry.target: Whether any player in the whole NCAA men's tournament reaches a single-game stat milestone (triple-double, 50+ points)
catalog_entry.mechanism: The event is a union over every player-game of the tournament (First Four included). Each player-game's chance is a far-tail probability of his stat distribution given minutes, usage, opponent and game script; exposure is the number of games his team survives. A few high-usage scorers or versatile rebound-and-assist players hold most of the mass, so the outcome depends on which teams make the field, how far they advance, star availability, blowout truncation, overtime and the stat source.

contract.settlement_definition: One binary per series per tournament. KXMARMAD3D: YES if any player records a triple-double (10+ in three or more of points, rebounds, assists, blocks, steals) in any game of the men's tournament scheduled Mar 17 to Apr 6, 2026. KXMARMADPTS: YES if any player scores 50+ points in a single game in the same tournament. First Four play-in games count for both. Rules do not name the stat source, do not address stat corrections after the game, and do not say whether overtime statistics count (normally they are part of the game box score).

rules_evidence.quote: Statistics that count towards a triple double include points, rebounds, assists, blocks, and steals. Any combination of 10+ in 3 or more of these statistics results in a triple-double.
rules_evidence.establishes: Five eligible categories; any three at 10+ settle YES, so points-rebounds-blocks counts as well as points-rebounds-assists.

rules_evidence.quote: For the purposes of this market, the first four play-in games are considered part of the men's college basketball tournament.
rules_evidence.establishes: First Four games are included, adding games and players from play-in teams to the union.

rules_evidence.quote: If any player records 50+ points in a game within the men's college basketball tournament originally scheduled from Mar 17, 2026 to Apr 6, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_evidence.establishes: Threshold is 50 or more points in one game by any player, aggregated over the whole tournament window.

variants_and_edge_cases: Two thresholds in one archetype: multi-category triple-double (KXMARMAD3D, floor_strike 1, any occurrence) and 50+ points (KXMARMADPTS, floor_strike 50).
Overtime: rules say 'in a game' without excluding overtime, so OT statistics presumably count; not explicitly stated.
Stat corrections by the official scorer after the game (an assist or rebound added or removed) are not addressed and can flip a 9 to a 10.
Tournament window and format are tied to the 2026 dates; a 2027 series under a changed field size would include a different number of games.

Games postponed outside the scheduled window: the wording 'originally scheduled from Mar 17, 2026 to Apr 6, 2026' suggests a postponed tournament game would still count, but the sampled text does not say; a cancelled tournament is not addressed.
contract.settlement_data_source: Not named in the rules; presumably official NCAA box scores. Source of truth and correction cut-off are unverified.

mechanism.summary: YES occurs if at least one player-game in the tournament crosses the threshold. For each player, the per-game probability is a far-tail quantity: 50 points requires a volume ceiling (about 30 field-goal attempts or many free throws), a hot shooting night and full minutes; a triple-double requires joint 10-counts in three of five stats and is mostly available to versatile guards or forwards (points-rebounds-assists) and elite rim protectors (points-rebounds-blocks). Exposure depends on which teams are in the field, how many games they survive (strong teams play more), and whether the star is healthy. Tournament games change the minutes distribution (shorter rotations in close games, blowouts in lopsided first-round games, occasional overtime) and opponent quality. The union over correlated player-games is concentrated on a few candidates, so tail calibration for them dominates, with settlement sensitive to official stat recording.

stages.name: Field composition and candidate pool
stages.description: Before Selection Sunday the pool of candidate players is uncertain because their teams may not receive bids; afterwards the field (68 teams with First Four, or a different number under a changed format) fixes who can play. Candidates are the small set of high-usage scorers and versatile multi-category producers, plus elite shot-blockers for points-rebounds-blocks triple-doubles.
stages.distribution: Candidate set is concentrated: perhaps 10 to 30 players carry most of the probability, with a long thin tail of others; bid probability is binary per team.

stages.name: Survival and exposure
stages.description: Each team plays until it loses, so expected games per player range from one (play-in losers count) to six or seven for finalists. Survival is shared by teammates, which correlates their chances, and depends on team strength and bracket path. Availability through March (injury, illness) multiplies exposure. During the tournament the same calculation is re-run on the live bracket: only surviving teams' remaining games count, and a recorded milestone ends the question.
stages.distribution: Games per player follow a truncated geometric-like distribution set by round-by-round win probabilities; strong-team stars have high exposure with a long right tail.

stages.name: Per-game minutes and game script
stages.description: Minutes in tournament games differ from the regular season: close elimination games push stars toward 38 to 40 minutes and occasional overtime adds five, while 1-versus-16 style blowouts pull stars early. Foul trouble in physical tournament officiating can cap minutes. Milestones are far-tail events, so these volume shifts have outsized effects.
stages.distribution: Minutes are a mixture of a close-game regime with a high ceiling and a blowout regime truncated at about 25 to 30 minutes; overtime adds a discrete +5 spike.

stages.name: Far-tail stat production
stages.description: Given minutes, a 50-point game requires extreme attempt volume and a hot shooting night against tournament-calibre defences; a triple-double requires correlated high counts in three stats. Per-game probabilities come from compound models with role-pooled tails and joint covariance, adjusted for opponent defence by role and for a possible neutral-site scorekeeper effect on recorded assists and rebounds, whose size is unmeasured (mile_u2).
stages.distribution: Compound overdispersed counts with heavy right tails; per-game 50+ probabilities for even elite scorers are well below 1 percent, triple-double probabilities a few percent at most for top versatile players.

stages.name: Union across player-games and settlement
stages.description: The settled event is the union over all player-games: one minus the probability that none hits. Shared survival paths and shared game scripts correlate player-games. Settlement counts First Four games and five triple-double categories; stat source and corrections are unspecified, and rebound and assist recording at the margin of 10 can decide the outcome.
stages.distribution: Binary and rare: 50-point tournament games and tournament triple-doubles occur in only a minority of tournaments in the modern era, so the prior for 50+ is small and for a triple-double modest; the exact historical counts are to be established by the field-level base-rate input (mile_u5), and the union is dominated by top candidates and sensitive to their tail errors.

cbb.player_game_exposure_tournament.label: Expected tournament games per candidate player (field entry x team survival x availability)
cbb.player_game_exposure_tournament.mechanism: A player can only hit a milestone in games his team plays; expected exposure is the sum over rounds of P(team in field) times P(team reaches that round) times P(player active).
cbb.player_game_exposure_tournament.rationale: Total team-games in the tournament are fixed by the format, but they concentrate on strong teams; a star on a 1 seed averages several games, a star on a 16 seed one or two. Subtle: the First Four counts, so play-in teams add a game, and a changed field size changes the count. The market trades through the tournament window, so exposure must be recomputed as teams are eliminated and as a milestone either occurs (settling YES) or becomes unreachable with fewer games left.
cbb.player_game_exposure_tournament.measurement: For each player as of t: E[games] = sum_r P(team bid) * P(team plays round r | bid) * P(player active in r), using the bracket simulation with fundamentals-only ratings; P(active) from injury status and star injury risk; before Selection Sunday include bid probability; report full distribution of games (1 to 7, or more under an expanded field). In-tournament state: after the field is set, condition on the live bracket at t (teams still alive, games already played, results to date) and set P(YES) = 1 for the relevant series once any qualifying game is final; remaining exposure = games still to be played by surviving teams only.
raw_data: bracket simulation output: team, round, probability
player-team roster mapping
availability status by date
cbb.player_game_exposure_tournament.why: Exposure weights each player's per-game milestone probability in the any-player union.

cbb.player_scoring_tail_index.label: Player single-game scoring right-tail index (probability of 40+ and 50+ point games)
cbb.player_scoring_tail_index.mechanism: A 50-point game sits far beyond typical college means, so its probability depends on the right tail of the player's game scoring distribution, driven by volume ceiling (shot attempts, free-throw trips) and hot shooting.
cbb.player_scoring_tail_index.rationale: Mean and sd from a negative binomial understate extreme tails for high-usage shooters and overstate them for efficient interior scorers. Subtle: extreme games usually combine high attempts, a hot three-point night and extra minutes (overtime), so the tail is a compound of several stages, not a single scale parameter.
cbb.player_scoring_tail_index.measurement: Per player: fit a compound model points = minutes x usage-based attempts x points per attempt with Beta-uncertain shooting and NB attempt dispersion, on the last 2 seasons of game logs; validate tail mass against observed 35+/40+ frequencies of D1 players pooled by role (generalised Pareto fit above 30 points, threshold chosen by mean-excess plot); output P(points >= 50 | game played) with credible interval. Attempt volume is scaled by the ratio of matchup expected possessions (cbb.tempo) to the possessions of the player's logged games.
raw_data: player game logs: minutes, FGA, 3PA, FTA, points
player usage and role
historical D1 30+ point games
cbb.player_scoring_tail_index.why: Per-game probability of the 50-point event for each candidate scorer.

cbb.triple_double_joint_propensity.label: Player per-game triple-double propensity across points, rebounds, assists, blocks and steals
cbb.triple_double_joint_propensity.mechanism: A triple-double needs 10+ in three of five categories in one game, which depends on the player's joint distribution of these counts given minutes, not their marginal means.
cbb.triple_double_joint_propensity.rationale: Points-rebounds-assists versatile guards and forwards and points-rebounds-blocks rim protectors are the realistic candidates; the joint probability is driven by positive correlation through minutes and pace and by negative correlation between assists and rebounds for some roles. Subtle: near misses (8-9 in a third category) are far more frequent and are the most informative for calibration.
cbb.triple_double_joint_propensity.measurement: Per player: simulate 5-category counts with NB marginals conditioned on a shared minutes draw and a Gaussian copula of residual correlations (from player stat covariance shrunk to role with n/(n+40)); count share of simulated games with >=3 categories at 10+; calibrate against observed D1 triple-double and 'two 10s plus 8+' frequencies over the last 5 seasons; as-of: prior games only. Counts are scaled by the same matchup-possessions ratio before the copula draw.
free_sources: Sports-Reference player game logs (single-game finder is a paid Stathead product; coverage start unverified)
raw_data: player box scores: points, rebounds, assists, blocks, steals, minutes
role classification
cbb.triple_double_joint_propensity.why: Per-game probability of a triple-double for each candidate across the five eligible stats.

cbb.milestone_union_aggregation.label: Any-player union over all tournament player-games with dependence
cbb.milestone_union_aggregation.mechanism: YES = at least one player-game hits the milestone; probability is one minus the probability that none does, computed over correlated player-games in a bracket where survival paths are shared.
cbb.milestone_union_aggregation.rationale: Simple independence summation overstates YES when probability is concentrated on a few stars whose games are correlated by team survival, and the chance that a candidate's team loses early removes several of his games at once. Subtle: the event is dominated by a handful of players, so the union is sensitive to errors in their tails, and 'long tail' depth (many players at very small probabilities) still contributes.
cbb.milestone_union_aggregation.measurement: Monte Carlo: simulate the bracket (with First Four) N >= 50,000 times; for each simulated game draw active players' stat lines from their per-game models (minutes linked to game margin and OT); YES if any line hits the milestone; report P(YES) and the contribution share of the top 10 players; compare with the analytical 1 - prod(1 - p_i)^{E[games_i]} as a check.
free_sources: Derived from bracket simulation and player models
raw_data: per-player per-game milestone probabilities
bracket simulation paths
game margin and OT simulation
cbb.milestone_union_aggregation.why: Converts per-player tails into the field-wide event the contract settles on.

cbb.elimination_game_star_minutes.label: Star minutes ceiling in single-elimination tournament games
cbb.elimination_game_star_minutes.mechanism: In elimination games coaches shorten rotations and play stars close to the full 40 minutes in close games, while lopsided first-round games cut star minutes.
cbb.elimination_game_star_minutes.rationale: Milestones need volume; a star's minutes distribution in the tournament differs from the regular season, with more 38+ minute games in close contests and longer media timeouts in televised tournament games giving extra rest. Subtle: overtime adds five minutes at a time and appears more often in close tournament games.
cbb.elimination_game_star_minutes.measurement: From the last 10 tournaments: for each team's top two usage players, minutes distribution in tournament games versus their own regular-season distribution, split by final margin bucket (0-5, 6-12, 13+); estimate shift in mean and in P(minutes >= 38); apply per candidate via role and coach rotation length.
raw_data: tournament box scores with minutes
regular-season player minutes
final margins
cbb.elimination_game_star_minutes.why: Volume of minutes is the multiplier on every tail rate; the tournament changes it.

cbb.tournament_field_milestone_base_rate.label: Field-level tournament base rate of 50-point games and triple-doubles by era
cbb.tournament_field_milestone_base_rate.mechanism: The any-player event is a rare count over about 67 team-games (more player-games), so the historical per-tournament frequency of 50+ point games and triple-doubles, adjusted for era, is a direct calibration anchor for the bottom-up union.
cbb.tournament_field_milestone_base_rate.rationale: Per-player tail models extrapolate far beyond their data; a field-level anchor bounds them. Era matters: the shot clock (35 s from 1993-94, 30 s from 2015-16), the three-point line and its 2019-20 move back, and tournament size changed scoring volume and the number of games, and stat-recording practice for assists and rebounds changed. Subtle: with so few events per decade the anchor is a wide interval, not a point, and it must not be tuned to the 2026 outcome.
cbb.tournament_field_milestone_base_rate.measurement: Count, per tournament year since 1985 (all rounds, play-in games from 2011), the number of player-games with 50+ points and with three 10+ categories among points, rebounds, assists, blocks and steals (blocks and steals only where recorded); events per 1,000 player-games with minutes above 25; Beta-Binomial posterior per era block (pre-1994, 1994-2014, 2015-present) with a Beta(0.5, 500) weakly informative prior; anchor P(YES in one tournament) = 1 - (1 - r_era)^(player-games with minutes above 25 in the target format), reported with its 90 percent interval and compared with the bottom-up cbb.milestone_union_aggregation output; as-of: tournaments completed before the pricing date only.
free_sources: Sports-Reference tournament box scores (coverage start unverified)
raw_data: tournament player-game box scores by year with minutes and the five stats
era table: shot-clock length, three-point distance, field size
cbb.tournament_field_milestone_base_rate.why: Gives a field-level frequency bound on the any-player union for both KXMARMADPTS (50+) and KXMARMAD3D (triple-double).

cbb.bracket_sim.reason: Survival paths determine how many games each candidate plays and correlate teammates; the union cannot be computed without it.

cbb.tournament_field_format.reason: Fixes the number of team-games (First Four included); a field-size change for 2027 would shift exposure for low seeds.

cbb.player_usage.reason: Usage and per-minute rates set the scale of each candidate's tails but not their shape, which the tail inputs model.

cbb.player_stat_covariance.reason: Joint covariance of counts is essential for triple-doubles; it lacks blocks and steals in its 4x4 definition, so it must be extended to five categories.

cbb.star_injury_risk.reason: A top candidate's absence removes a large share of the union mass; matters most for the few dominant candidates.

cbb.blowout_garbage.reason: Its catalog measurement computes P(|margin| > 15/20/25) by spread, a market line; use only as a comparison for the fundamentals-based cbb.margin_regime_mixture driven by cbb.ratings_fundamentals expected margin.

cbb.ot_model.reason: Its catalog measurement is empirical OT frequency by closing spread and total bucket, which are market values; overtime chance here comes from the market-free cbb.ot_period_tie_chain instead.

cbb.opp_stat_allowed.reason: Tournament opponents are stronger than the season average, lowering tails; useful as an adjustment rather than a primary driver.

cbb.box_score_source_risk.reason: Rebound and assist recording near 10 can decide a triple-double; the source is not named in the rules so provider disagreement is a real risk.

m.rules_text.reason: Defines First Four inclusion, the five eligible categories and the tournament window; must be re-read for each season's series.

cbb.margin_regime_mixture.reason: Defined on model expected margins independent of closing lines; gives the blowout-regime probability that truncates star minutes in lopsided early-round games.

cbb.ot_period_tie_chain.reason: Market-free P(regulation tie) and OT-period probabilities give extra star minutes; its pregame expected-total term must be taken from model possessions, not a posted total.

cbb.coach_blowout_substitution_rate.reason: Play-by-play based starter-pull and lead-protection rate per coach; turns a blowout regime into minutes lost by candidates, with no market input.

cbb.tempo.reason: Expected matchup possessions rescale volume for every candidate, a first-order driver of far-tail counts that minutes and usage alone miss; tournament pace is often set by the slower team.

cbb.teammate_absence_shift.reason: With/without splits show how a missing teammate redistributes usage, rebounds and assists to a candidate; star_injury_risk only covers the candidate's own absence.

interactions.mechanism: Each player's contribution to the union is roughly per-game tail probability times expected games; a volume scorer on a likely first-round loser adds little, while a moderate-tail star on a 1 seed adds more through five or six games.
interactions.how_to_test: Decompose the simulated union by player and compare with the product of tail probability and expected games; check against historical 40+ tournament games by seed.

interactions.mechanism: In close tournament games stars play near 40 minutes; in blowouts they sit early. The regime is set by the matchup's expected margin, so the minutes ceiling and tail probability switch between two levels rather than shifting smoothly.
interactions.how_to_test: Tournament minutes of top-usage players by final-margin bucket versus their regular-season minutes in the same buckets.

interactions.mechanism: Three counts reaching 10 together depend on shared minutes and pace and on role-specific residual correlation; the minutes draw links all categories, so a high-minutes regime raises triple-double probability more than proportionally.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare observed D1 triple-double frequencies with independent-marginal predictions and with copula predictions by minutes bucket.

interactions.mechanism: Teammates and opponents share survival paths: if a candidate's team loses early, his games and his teammates' games vanish together, so the union has less effective diversification than independent player-games imply.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare simulated P(YES) under full bracket correlation with an independence approximation using the same marginals.

interactions.mechanism: Overtime adds about 12 percent more minutes to a full-minute star; because the 50-point event is far in the tail, a modest minutes increase raises its probability by much more than 12 percent.
interactions.how_to_test: Frequency of 40+ point games in OT versus non-OT games for high-usage players, normalised by minutes.

interactions.mechanism: Possessions scale attempt volume, and the 50-point event sits far in the tail, so a fast matchup raises its probability by more than the possession ratio; a slow game controlled by the opponent pushes the same star far below the 50-point reach.
interactions.how_to_test: Frequency of 35+ point games by matchup expected-possessions tercile for high-usage scorers, normalised by minutes.

nonlinearities.why: P(points >= 50) changes by orders of magnitude with small changes in usage and shooting variance; a normal tail assigns essentially zero, a fitted heavy tail does not, so tail shape dominates the estimate.

nonlinearities.shape: concave in per-round win probability through compounding
nonlinearities.why: Expected games equal one plus the cumulative product of round win probabilities, so improving an already strong team adds games at a diminishing rate, while a weak team's exposure is pinned near one.
With many small per-game probabilities the union is almost additive, but when a dominant candidate has a large probability the union saturates and other players add less.
